summary: Popular machine learning algorithms written from scratch in Python, with the math explained and interactive Jupyter demos.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Homemade Machine Learning implements classic machine learning algorithms in plain Python so you can see how they work, rather than calling a library one-liner. It covers linear and logistic regression, k-means clustering, anomaly detection with a Gaussian distribution and a multilayer perceptron neural network. Each algorithm has the math explained and a Jupyter demo where you can change the training data and settings and see the results and charts. Explanations mostly follow Andrew Ng's Coursera machine learning course.
sixtySeconds.problem: Library calls hide how algorithms actually work. Writing them from scratch with explanations helps you understand the math.
whoFor: Developers who want to understand the math
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Use it to learn core ML algorithms from the inside, with demos you can run in the browser.

overview: Open any demo in the browser with NBViewer to read it, or in Binder to edit and run it, with nothing to install.
To run locally, install the dependencies with pip install -r requirements.txt and start jupyter notebook.
The code is for learning, not production. MIT licensed.
